final_message: Implemented the split of the sync branches into project/<id>/sync/register and project/<id>/sync/exec-events. Added the new `sync` config with per-kind `branches` and kept legacy `register_sync` as a one-branch compatibility mode. Two plan items remain open because executor cannot write the files: the CI workflow (.github/workflows is denied) and the prj-0001 config migration. Proposals for both are in the ticket and in handoff.
handoff: Protected change proposal (needs user approval, feature branch): .github/workflows/check-register-push.yml. Add "project/*/sync/register" and "project/*/sync/exec-events" to on.push.branches, keeping "project/*/register" until migration completes. Change project extraction from `project="${project%/register}"` to `project="${project%%/*}"`. branch-check picks the branch scope from --remote-ref, so nothing else changes. Executor could not write .github/workflows/ (permission denied). Ticket work row 5 is left open for this.

Migration of prj-0001 from project/prj-0001/register to the two sync branches, to be done by the orchestrator when no run, queue or routine is active. (1) Publish any stopped sync with register branch-push. (2) Run register branch-merge on develop and push develop. (3) Create project/prj-0001/sync/register and project/prj-0001/sync/exec-events from the merged develop tip and push them. (4) Replace "register_sync": {"enabled": true} with "sync": {"enabled": true} in .specdojo/specdojo.config.json via a feature branch. (5) Check that register branch-push --project prj-0001 --dry-run reports both as already on origin, then remove the old dedicated worktree. (6) Delete the old branch once other users have switched. Ticket work row 9 is left open for this.

Decision recorded in the ticket: legacy `register_sync` is not aliased to `sync`. Aliasing would switch writes to not-yet-existing branches as soon as the CLI is upgraded. The switch therefore happens explicitly when the config changes. `sync` and `register_sync` together is a config error.

Decision recorded in the ticket: when one operation writes both branches, register goes first and exec-events second, one at a time and not nested (the lock is shared). A register failure stops before exec-events. An exec-events failure keeps the published register bookkeeping, and recovery is `register branch-push --sync exec-events` followed by a retry. No current operation writes both.
CHANGELOG lines (Added / Migration notes) are drafted in the ticket's response section 'CHANGELOG に書く事項' per the playbook rule (PJR-EPQ3). CHANGELOG.md was not edited.
